questions.question: On a Level 3 drawing, a pipe is labelled “PEX.” What does this normally mean?
questions.explanation: PEX means cross-linked polyethylene. It is commonly used for potable water and some hydronic applications when approved.

questions.category: C3 — Use Codes, Regulations and Standards
questions.question: What is the main purpose of the National Plumbing Code of Canada?
options: To provide minimum plumbing safety and health requirements
To allow any material in any system
questions.explanation: The NPC sets minimum requirements for safe plumbing systems. It helps protect potable water, drainage performance, public health, and buildings.

questions.question: When installing a building sewer, what is most critical for proper operation?
options: Correct slope, bedding, alignment, and approved connection
Pipe colour and label direction only
Maximum number of elbows regardless of flow
questions.explanation: Sewers depend on gravity flow and proper support. Poor bedding, reverse slope, or misalignment can cause settlement and blockages.

questions.question: A water service enters a building from underground. What must be protected where freezing is possible?
questions.explanation: Water service piping can freeze and burst if not protected. Burial depth, insulation, heat, and routing must be considered.

questions.category: I2 — Install Potable Water Distribution Systems
questions.question: What is the purpose of a pressure-reducing valve in a water distribution system?
questions.explanation: A PRV lowers high supply pressure to protect fixtures and piping. Excess pressure can cause leaks, noise, and premature failure.
